incompatibility: UNB-EXP-002 requires the public identity to be branded 'Unbound'. REQ-X-057 requires white-label multi-sponsor channels, and INV-18 requires the legally responsible sponsoring charity to be disclosed. A single 'Unbound' public identity cannot also be each partner sponsor's brand, and it may misidentify the legal sponsor.
objective_a: Distinct, independently branded reference enterprise demonstrating EF.
objective_b: One platform serving many legal sponsors under their own brands, with truthful legal-sponsor disclosure.
alternatives: (a) 'Unbound' is the platform name, never shown as sponsor; (b) 'Unbound' is the synthetic reference sponsor only; (c) both, with brand-layer rules.
recommended_resolution: (c): 'Unbound' names the platform and the synthetic reference sponsor. Production channels show the partner sponsor brand, with a mandatory non-configurable legal-sponsor disclosure. Amend UNB-EXP-002 accordingly.
tradeoffs: Loses a single consumer brand in partner channels, but avoids misleading sponsor identity.

incompatibility: CHARTER requires at least three operating models to be compared on identical scenarios before the gate, and the gate authorizes architecture. REQ-X-057 fixes the architecture by owner decision and rejects any alternative deployable before that comparison.
objective_a: Evidence-based selection among materially different operating models.
objective_b: Coherent, non-fragmented single system across commercial channels.
alternatives: (a) Amend CHARTER to recognise REQ-X-057 as a fixed constraint; (b) run the autonomy-model comparison as policy configurations inside one system; (c) suspend REQ-X-057 until the comparison is done.
recommended_resolution: (a)+(b): keep REQ-X-057 as an owner constraint, and redefine the CHARTER comparison as autonomy/organization models expressed through sponsor policy and authority tiers in the one system.
tradeoffs: Gives up evaluating architecture alternatives, but keeps comparing organizational models, which matters more for risk.

incompatibility: REQ-X-008: death does not cancel sponsor-approved unpaid grants, and future instructions suspend until successor authority is verified. FM-05 says to 'cancel or suspend pending actions'. UNB-SUCC-008 suspends former authority only at succession activation. ADM-022 calls for 'evidence-driven suspension'. Taken together they give three different suspension times and two dispositions for pending grants.
objective_a: Honor the sponsor's own completed decisions and avoid stranding charities.
objective_b: Fail-safe stop of actions whose authority has lapsed.
alternatives: (a) Complete approved grants and suspend the rest; (b) hold all for review; (c) cancel all unpaid; (d) per-sponsor policy parameter.
recommended_resolution: (d), with suspension of donor-derived rights at verified death (not activation) and no default until OD-03 is answered. Amend FM-05 to 'suspend', reserving 'cancel' for an authorized decision.
tradeoffs: Configurability adds testing burden, but avoids encoding an unanswered legal question.

incompatibility: REQ-X-057 requires a single coordinated deployment and rejects a second deployable. UNB-TEN-002 requires dedicated-database and dedicated-infrastructure partner profiles.
objective_a: Avoid fragmentation and duplicated financial state.
objective_b: Contractual tenant isolation up to dedicated infrastructure.
alternatives: (a) 'One' = one codebase and model, N instances; (b) drop profile C; (c) profile C as a protective-only exception ADR.
recommended_resolution: (a): define 'one system' as one artifact, one domain model, one release train and one ledger contract per legal sponsor. Instances may be separate. Prohibit forks, not instances.
tradeoffs: Operating N instances costs more, but keeps the isolation promise.

incompatibility: REQ-X-061 requires secure deletion and retention boundaries when a sponsor exits. UNB-DATA-001 forbids DELETE of committed authoritative records, and UNB-DATA-008 forbids administrators from rewriting history. In shared-database profiles with cross-tenant integrity checkpoints, deleting a tenant could break integrity verification for other tenants.
objective_a: Honor contractual data return and deletion at exit.
alternatives: (a) Per-tenant encryption keys with cryptographic erasure after handover and retention expiry; (b) hand records over to the sponsor and retain nothing; (c) retain under legal hold only.
recommended_resolution: (a)+(b): integrity chains and checkpoints are tenant-scoped. At exit, export a verified package, retain for the contractual and legal period, then destroy per-tenant keys under dual control with an exit certificate. Counsel confirms the retention period.
tradeoffs: Per-tenant key management and chain partitioning add complexity.

requirement_b: the wave 2 conversion file next action 5
incompatibility: Step 0 says 'Complete this step before any further mission work'. Wave 2 says requirements analysis 'may continue without falsely claiming installation'. That permits the very work step 0 forbids.
objective_a: Ensure all mission work is done under the verified EF toolchain.
objective_b: Allow requirements discovery to proceed while bootstrap is blocked.
alternatives: (a) Owner waiver for requirements-only work; (b) execute bootstrap; (c) treat post-step-0 artifacts as provisional.
recommended_resolution: (a)+(c) now, (b) before any architecture.
tradeoffs: Accepts that the EF experiment baseline was missing for these artifacts.

incompatibility: REQ-X-009 requires a receivable on returned contributions; the REQ-X-084 example A debits a 'sponsor-approved return/reversal account' and TX-05 a 'compensating debit'.
objective_a: Preserve the claim and exposure created when provisionally credited value funded grants.
objective_b: Avoid presuming a legally enforceable donor claim; use a sponsor policy account.
alternatives: (a) donor receivable with allowance; (b) contribution reversal with sponsor loss; (c) neutral exposure fact with policy-selected posting.
recommended_resolution: (c): record a typed ReturnedContributionExposure fact; CPA policy selects the posting; counsel decides whether any claim against the donor exists; OD-20 decides the loss-bearer.
tradeoffs: (c) adds a policy step but avoids booking unenforceable receivables.

incompatibility: CANONICAL posts an in-entity sponsor fee as interfund (no cash leaves); fixtures JRN-06/07 and example D settle Fee Payable against Cash.
objective_a: Correct consolidated sponsor books with eliminations.
alternatives: (a) always interfund; (b) always payable/cash; (c) by fee-recipient type.
recommended_resolution: (c): a fee-recipient discriminator selects interfund for sponsor-internal fees and payable/cash for third parties.
tradeoffs: More posting rules, but each is correct for its case.

incompatibility: ACC-MDL-009 blocks close on any unexplained break; UNB-NAV-007 blocks NAV publication only on material unexplained breaks; REQ-X-040 auto-validates routine items under materiality.
objective_b: Operability: immaterial noise must not halt NAV or close.
alternatives: (a) zero tolerance; (b) materiality only; (c) three-tier tolerance/materiality/aging.
recommended_resolution: (c): rounding tolerance auto-clears with evidence; material breaks block the affected scope; immaterial unexplained breaks do not block but must be resolved within an aging limit, and certification discloses them.
tradeoffs: Requires threshold governance; avoids both paralysis and silent acceptance.

incompatibility: REQ-X-010 requires independent reviewer attestation of reconciliations; REQ-X-040 lets routine deterministic reconciliations auto-pass.
alternatives: (a) attest every reconciliation; (b) attest nothing routine; (c) attest the policy and exceptions.
recommended_resolution: (c): an independent reviewer approves matching rules and tolerances (versioned), every exception resolution, and the period close certification; deterministic passes are recorded evidence.
tradeoffs: Relies on control over rule changes (CTL-010); auditors may require sample testing.

incompatibility: REQ-X-023 makes unitization optional; FI-02, CTL-018 and the capacity formula V(f,t) are unit-based.
objective_b: A single computable capacity and ledger invariant.
alternatives: (a) unitize everything; (b) generalize valuation to positions.
recommended_resolution: (b): V(f,t) = sum of position valuations under the declared valuation policy per holding type; units x NAV is the pooled case.
tradeoffs: Slightly more complex formula; keeps sponsor choice.

incompatibility: The REQ-X-084 schema places FundId on the batch header; the CANONICAL envelope and multi-fund journals (successor split, interfund fee) need line-level funds.
alternatives: (a) header fund and split into linked journals; (b) line-level fund only.
recommended_resolution: (b), with fund as a balancing segment.
tradeoffs: None material.

incompatibility: ACC-MDL-004 and REQ-X-084 define capacity as a projection (rebuildable per UNB-NAV-044); REQ-X-022 and FI-05 need capacity checked transactionally with the reservation.
alternatives: (a) synchronous derived computation in the reservation transaction; (b) async projection with compensation.
recommended_resolution: (a): derived but computed from authoritative state inside the serializable reservation transaction; the async projection is display-only.
tradeoffs: Higher write-path cost; correctness guaranteed.

incompatibility: UNB-GFUND-011 implies per-grant liquidation with tax-lot rules; FI-14 has pools redeem units internally and trade net.
objective_a: Explain the funding of each grant.
objective_b: Efficient pool operations and correct unit accounting.
alternatives: (a) per-grant trades; (b) by source type.
recommended_resolution: (b): unit redemption for pool sources, trade instructions only for segregated sources.
tradeoffs: The donor sees units redeemed, not securities sold, for pooled sources.

incompatibility: Profile C requires a dedicated partner deployment with its own authoritative store; REQ-X-057 and its acceptance item 7 reject any second deployable or ledger.
objective_b: Single coherent product with one financial truth and no forks
alternatives: (a) Define one system = one codebase/release/domain model; allow N identical cells; (b) drop Profile C; (c) dedicated infrastructure only for storage, shared runtime
recommended_resolution: (a) with explicit cell definition and inter-cell protocol; Profile C activated only on contract
tradeoffs: (a) keeps both objectives but adds inter-cell messaging; (b) loses institutional deals; (c) weak isolation story for regulators

incompatibility: Global hold/payment release serialization point cannot exist as one transaction when holds are global and releases are in separate partner databases.
objective_a: No payment to a recipient after a durable hold
alternatives: (a) synchronous fail-closed hold check against a global registry at release; (b) replicated hold watermark fence per cell; (c) copy holds into each cell transactionally via outbox and block releases until acknowledged
recommended_resolution: (b) plus (a) as fallback: release records observed global hold version and requires it to equal the registry's current version read in the same gate
tradeoffs: (a) availability coupling to registry; (b) replication lag can pause releases; (c) complex

incompatibility: Single authoritative transaction for multi-component financial operations versus one sponsor's funds spread over several partner stores, with cross-partner transfers explicitly non-transactional.
objective_b: Partner segregation within one legal sponsor
alternatives: (a) partition ledger by legal sponsor, not partner; (b) saga with suspense account and reconciliation; (c) forbid one sponsor across multiple partner stores
recommended_resolution: (a) where contracts allow; otherwise (b) with zero-sum daily control
tradeoffs: (a) weakens partner-level physical separation; (b) adds pending states visible to donors

incompatibility: All documents SHALL use Folio versus Typst as preferred PDF renderer for issued documents.
alternatives: (a) Folio P2 Chromium for all; (b) Typst for issued PDFs, Folio for HTML views; (c) both behind adapter
recommended_resolution: ADR with fixture benchmark; choose one issuance renderer
tradeoffs: (c) doubles template and accessibility work

incompatibility: Strata mandated with append-only guarantees versus persistence/event-sourcing choice ADR-gated.
alternatives: (a) Strata for schema lifecycle only; (b) remove mandate; (c) extend Strata
tradeoffs: (c) turns a pilot schema tool into a database product

incompatibility: Humans required for grant decisions versus zero-touch deterministic approval of routine grants.
alternatives: (a) board-delegated deterministic policy counts as sponsor decision (OD-01 yes); (b) batch human approval; (c) per-grant human
recommended_resolution: Await OD-01; reword AIN-003 to carve out board-delegated deterministic policy and forbid AI approval
tradeoffs: (c) removes automation benefit; (a) needs counsel and board

incompatibility: Nonwaivable universal seven-year floor versus 'do not invent universal retention periods'.
alternatives: (a) keep floor as platform law; (b) floor as default sponsor-contract parameter; (c) per-class counsel schedule only
recommended_resolution: (b) with (c) overriding per class
tradeoffs: (a) over-retains PII; (c) slower to finalise

incompatibility: Platform keeps financial records seven years regardless of sponsor offboarding versus sponsor-owned evidence-complete export and portability with lawful deletion.
objective_b: Sponsor data ownership and processor obligations
alternatives: (a) platform escrow by contract; (b) transfer custody to sponsor with attestation and delete; (c) both selectable
recommended_resolution: (c) defined in sponsor contract; counsel on controller/processor roles
tradeoffs: (a) platform liability and cost; (b) relies on sponsor

incompatibility: Tenancy forbids shared-schema row-level model by default while ordering acceptance tests assume a shared database with tenant predicates.
alternatives: (a) rewrite ADV-079 for schema binding; (b) approve row-level as fourth profile
tradeoffs: (b) widens attack surface

incompatibility: Dashboards, widgets and report designer deferred versus Work Queue dashboards first-class now.
alternatives: (a) defer both; (b) build minimal exception inbox now, dashboards later
tradeoffs: Some supervisor visibility deferred

incompatibility: Distinct failed/uncertain states required, but screen contracts define no Unknown/Failed state.
alternatives: (a) add Unknown/Failed to UI set; (b) separate UI loading states from domain states
tradeoffs: Slightly more design work per screen

incompatibility: WCAG 2.2 AA plus legal obligations versus document accessibility only 'where supported'.
alternatives: (a) tagged PDF required; (b) accessible HTML equivalent from same snapshot; (c) on-request alternative format
recommended_resolution: (b) as baseline, (a) when renderer proves it
tradeoffs: (c) alone may be insufficient legally (counsel)

requirement_a: REQ-X-057 (one queue, no queue per function)
incompatibility: One work orchestration with no per-function queues versus department role workspaces each with own queue.
alternatives: (a) one Case/WorkItem store with role filters; (b) per-department queues
tradeoffs: Requires good routing metadata

incompatibility: UNB-GRANT-048 requires human approval of every material grant modification after sponsor approval. REQ-X-017 has deterministic policy resolve routine cases with no human touch, and REQ-X-001 has a material change invalidate approval so it is re-decided by the same routing.
objective_a: Make sure an accountable human sees changes made after approval.
objective_b: Remove routine manual work while preserving independence.
alternatives: (a) Human approves every material modification. (b) The modification invalidates approval and is re-routed through Tier 1/2/3. (c) A human approves only modifications above configured materiality.
recommended_resolution: (b): a material modification is a new decision under REQ-X-017. Use the human tier only when the deterministic gates hold or refer. Materiality classes are sponsor policy (L3).
tradeoffs: (b) depends on OD-01 validation of delegated approval. Until then, sponsors without delegation fall back to (a).

incompatibility: UNB-GRANT-012 routes human approvals by role, amount, risk and relationship as the default model. REQ-X-017 makes deterministic sponsor-delegated policy the first tier for every case.
alternatives: (a) Keep human routing as the default. (b) Treat human routing as Tier 3 only. (c) Hybrid by sponsor.
recommended_resolution: (b), with UNB-GRANT-012 restated as the Tier 3 routing matrix. The existence of Tier 1 for each sponsor is gated by OD-01.
tradeoffs: Sponsors that have not adopted board delegation keep human approval, so there are two operating modes to test.

incompatibility: UNB-CHAR-023 allows sponsor-specific eligibility overrides within lawful policy. REQ-X-018 layer L2 and ADV-053 forbid sponsors from weakening common vetting.
objective_a: Let sponsors exercise their own judgment, for example for churches or new charities.
objective_b: Keep one common safety floor and prevent sponsor-level weakening.
alternatives: (a) Allow overrides, scoped to the sponsor. (b) Forbid all overrides. (c) Sponsor-supplied evidence goes through the common alternate-verification path. Overrides are allowed only for sponsor-overlay (L3) restrictions, never against a common Ineligible or HeldAdverse status.
recommended_resolution: (c). UNB-CHAR-023 is limited to L3 grant-policy overlays. Evidence gaps are closed through UNB-RCN-GRT-013.
tradeoffs: A sponsor waits for common verification instead of acting alone, which is slower for edge cases.

incompatibility: REQ-X-007 sends adverse findings to all affected sponsors. UNB-CHAR-036 (with UNB-EXT-033 and CHAR-T10) keeps sponsor-specific investigations separate.
objective_a: Every sponsor is protected from a known-bad charity.
objective_b: Sponsor confidentiality, due process and protection against defamation.
alternatives: (a) Share full evidence. (b) Share nothing. (c) Share a typed status and reason class without the evidence. A global hold requires E0/E1 evidence or independent compliance authority.
recommended_resolution: (c). Add a RaiseGlobalHold command that requires independent authority, evidence class E0 or E1, and a review SLA. Sponsor-private allegations stay as sponsor overlay holds.
tradeoffs: Other sponsors cannot see why a charity is held. Raising a global hold takes longer.

incompatibility: REQ-X-007 and gate G03 set one 180-day validity for all common evidence. UNB-RULE-015 and REQ-X-018 (POLICY-PRECEDENCE line 124) require freshness by fact, jurisdiction and risk, with no universal number.
objective_a: A simple uniform cycle that is easy to audit.
objective_b: Proportionate freshness: shorter for volatile facts and longer for static ones.
alternatives: (a) Universal 180 days. (b) A freshness table by fact type with the comprehensive review as one row. (c) Only per-sponsor values.
recommended_resolution: (b). The 180-day value becomes the proposed maximum age for the comprehensive-review bundle, subject to counsel approval.
tradeoffs: A larger configuration surface that needs governance.

requirement_b: NACHA Notification of Change obligation (external network rule; not a repo requirement)
incompatibility: REQ-X-005 and REQ-X-083 invariant 2 require an independently authorized destination change and a pinned destination version. ACH network rules require the originator to apply NOC corrections within a set period (the current rule text must be checked).
alternatives: (a) Ignore NOCs until full independent verification. (b) Apply NOCs automatically. (c) Classify an NOC as RDFI-originated E1 evidence with expedited verification, and hold entries until the new version is effective.
tradeoffs: Short payment delays to recipients with an NOC.

incompatibility: REQ-X-002 reserves currency atomically at approval against net capacity. UNB-GFUND-011 and UNB-GFUND-013 fund grants by later liquidation with value-lock policies, so the currency does not exist at approval.
objective_a: No overcommitment and no external commitment without funding.
objective_b: Allow grants funded from invested assets without forced pre-sale.
alternatives: (a) Sell before approval. (b) Reserve units with a haircut and an ApprovedPendingLiquidity state. (c) Reserve dollars and absorb the shortfall from a sponsor-defined waterfall.
recommended_resolution: (b), with an explicit shortfall rule. No external commitment is made until liquidity settles.
tradeoffs: More states. Recipients see approval before any cash commitment.

incompatibility: REQ-X-018 gate G05 rejects pledges globally. UNB-GRANT-011 evaluates pledges and escalates uncertain cases, and daf-landscape WL-09 plus Notice 2017-73 allow pledge-related distributions under conditions.
objective_b: Respect lawful sponsor choice and IRS reliance guidance.
alternatives: (a) Global prohibition. (b) Sponsor L3 policy with values Prohibited/NonBindingOnly/NoticeConditions on a counsel baseline. (c) Case-by-case human review.
tradeoffs: Sponsor configurations differ, and the pledge-reference suppression must be enforced.

incompatibility: TX-13 has one target state, ProviderUnknownOrAccepted. REQ-X-083 and REQ-X-004 require Unknown and Acknowledged to be separate, because Unknown blocks retry and reissue.
alternatives: (a) Keep the merged state. (b) Split it into two transitions.
recommended_resolution: (b). TX-16 (VoidOrReissuePending) must start only from known states.
tradeoffs: None material.

incompatibility: The event envelope makes sponsorId, partnerId and DAFId mandatory. REQ-X-007 requires platform-wide charity evidence events with no duplicate vetting per sponsor.
alternatives: (a) Copy the event per sponsor. (b) A platform scope class in the envelope.
tradeoffs: Authorization for the platform scope must be defined explicitly.

incompatibility: One coordinated deployment with one authoritative financial core versus three simultaneous isolation profiles (shared schema, separate schema or database, dedicated infrastructure), each requiring tenant-specific schema deployment, which Strata does not template.
alternatives: (a) all three profiles; (b) deployment cells of one release, sponsor as partition key; (c) database per sponsor only
recommended_resolution: (b): one codebase and release, N identical cells; release 1 has a single shared cell; dedicated cells only on cited contractual need (RCD-004)
tradeoffs: Dedicated-infrastructure buyers wait for a later release; much lower test and migration matrix

incompatibility: Folio is mandated for documents, yet REQ-X-033 specifies Typst rendering. Neither verifiably produces accessible (tagged) PDFs, and Typst is outside the Echelon component set.
alternatives: Folio P2 deterministic Chromium; Typst; accessible HTML statement with archived PDF rendition
recommended_resolution: Spike plus ADR (RCD-009). Keep hashing and signing renderer-independent in the document registry.
tradeoffs: Spike cost versus risk of inaccessible statements
